I hope this nonsense is not being dredged up again. This article is over a year old and the issue had no legs because there was no boogeyman to run from. The new NSPS rules are all about manufacturer requirements, not coming to your home with swat team to take your stove.

Hmm. The article failed to cover a couple important questions. Can the grandfathered stoves be transferred in private sales? Is the technology to manufacture compliant stoves current feasible? Does the 13% percent of the nations soot the current stoves output marjorly affect areas of high population?

This. Especially this part of the article needed way more information.

The whole point of the EPA’s proposed regulations, however, is that there are not currently stoves that pass the emissions test. That is why the rules would take time to implement — to give manufacturers time to comply.

I think it's key to the legislation in question. Is compliance possible within a reasonable sales cost for people who currently use wood-burning stoves? A lot of them are very poor. If their stove breaks and new ones cost too much, and they can't afford a whole new heating system they will indeed freeze.

And ultimately the amount (and type) of particulates generated by wood-burning stoves is of relatively little environmental significance. What we really need is easing of constraints for new nuclear power plants and fewer nuclear NIMBYs. That would massively cut particle emissions.
